doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Attraction to the jazz masters, Billy Cobham and joining Sonny Rollins
summary: Soskin says he preferred Sonny Rollins to fusion, which he was tied to only through touring with Billy Cobham; he joined Rollins around 1977-78 in his early twenties with full confidence.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah, we’re going to talk about that, I have some questions about that. I wanted to go back a little bit to the early 70s and from what I read about you you were studying classical music but attracted to jazz. And when I think of the early 70s I mean jazz fusion and jazz rock was in full bloom.
So I’m wondering, the jazz that you were attracted to and maybe pulled you away from classical, was it jazz fusion or was it more like the masters, the —

Yeah it was more of the masters. You know jazz, the only reason I’m associated with jazz fusion was because of Billy Cobham. And at that time Billy Cobham was very popular and so we used to tour a lot. But I was really into, I don’t know, Sonny Rollins. You know that’s what I really liked to do. So you know I went from there to playing with Sonny.
How would — you would have been in your early twenties?
Well we’re talking about like 1977, 78. Yes. My early twenties.
Were you thinking to yourself, questioning whether you were in over your head?
No, no. I always knew what I was doing and hopefully still do.
